newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Consob okays HPI bourse listing - sources.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Consob okays HPI bourse listing - sources.

text.p: Italian stock market regulator Consob has approved new holding company HPI's prospectus and given its go-ahead for a bourse listing of ordinary and savings shares of the firm which groups the industrial activities of financial holding Gemina, Consob sources said.
Consob's green light for the listing was an essential first step as only bourse listed companies can have savings shares.
Gemina last year decided to spin off its industrial operations into the new company, Holding di Partecipazioni Industriali SpA (HPI).
After the formal spin-off the prospectus will be published and Consob will set the date for a bourse quotation.

Earlier this month, the stock market evaluated HPI ordinary shares at 1,050 lire and savings shares at 1,000 lire. Gemina, which is not bound by the evaluation, is offering 2.57 billion ordinary and 112.9 million non-convertible savings shares.
The stock market council has estimated HPI's total value at 2.815 trillion lire.
After the spin off is complete Gemina will be left with a clutch of financial assets.
